title: Arrange Tanks for Most Distinct Subarrays
statement:
There are `m` different types of tanks, numbered `1` to `m`, and you have an unlimited supply of each type. You must place exactly `n` tanks in a single row.

A contiguous block of the row (a subarray) is called **distinct** if no tank type appears more than once inside it. Two blocks at different positions are different subarrays even if they list the same types. Arrange the row so that the number of distinct subarrays is as large as possible. If several arrangements reach that maximum, print the **lexicographically smallest** one (compare the rows element by element as integers).

Print the arrangement as `n` integers, the tank type at each position.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers `m` and `n`: the number of tank types, then the number of tanks in the row.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers, the tank types of the chosen arrangement from left to right.

examples.explanation: With 3 types, a distinct subarray can have length at most 3. In 1 2 3 1 2 every window of 3 consecutive tanks has three different types, so all 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 subarrays of length 1 to 3 are distinct, which is the most possible. It is also the lexicographically smallest row that achieves this.
Only one tank is placed, and the smallest type is 1.
There are more types than tanks, so all three tanks can be different. All 6 subarrays are distinct, and 1 2 3 is the lexicographically smallest such row.

hints: A subarray cannot be distinct if it is longer than m. How many subarrays of each length can be distinct at best?
To make every subarray of length up to m distinct, every window of m consecutive tanks must contain m different types.
That forces the row to repeat with period m. Among such rows, which one is lexicographically smallest?
